advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make rotation prefer the just-written artifact when mtimes tie (e.g. exclude the new path from the eviction set or sort with a stable secondary key).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:288: existing = sorted(d.glob("*.json"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
path returned to the caller (line 291) and embedded in the error message (line 254) can point at a file that a same-tick eviction removed
advisory.finding: Rotation sorts `*.json` by `st_mtime` and evicts `existing[:-20]` after writing the new artifact; on filesystems with coarse mtime granularity a tie between the just-written file and pre-existing files resolves by glob/path order, so the newly written artifact could itself be the one evicted, silently discarding the reply the raised error names.
scenarios: A directory already at/over 20 artifacts on a low-resolution-mtime filesystem where the new write shares an mtime bucket with existing files.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the parameter-threading implementation with the ticket plan's `resolve_gate_config` in-branch approach (update the ticket or confirm the deviation is intended).
evidence: ticket 2fd6 Approach: 'The failure hook in structured_run.py obtains the resolved value on the failure path via rebar.llm.config.resolve_gate_config(...)'

ticket 2fd6 Alternatives considered: '(a) threading the dir down as a new _pai_structured parameter — heavier signature churn across callers ... The chosen in-branch resolve is the smallest correct change.'
src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:161-170 — added `*, artifact_dir: str | None = None` parameter; runner.py:537-546 resolves `cfg.parse_failure_artifact_dir` and forwards it
advisory.finding: The implementation threads `artifact_dir` as a new `_pai_structured` parameter and resolves it in the runner via `cfg.parse_failure_artifact_dir`, whereas the approved ticket plan explicitly specified reading the dir inside structured_run.py via `resolve_gate_config(...)` and REJECTED the parameter-threading approach as 'heavier signature churn across callers'.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer comparing the merged code against the certified plan finds the resolution seam moved.

evidence: config.py adds the loader binding: "REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR", "parse_failure_artifact_dir", None via _llm_str (src/rebar/llm/config.py:580-587)
New tests bypass the loader: `cfg = LLMConfig(repo_path="."); ... cfg.parse_failure_artifact_dir = str(artifact_dir)` (tests/unit/test_structured_run.py:60-62)

Sibling loader tests exist and DO cover analogous keys: tests/unit/test_config_llm.py:90 asserts `o.model_provider == 'anthropic' and o.base_url == 'https://local'` from a [tool.rebar.llm] table, and the _clean fixture lists REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL etc. (test_config_llm.py:29-46) — no equivalent assertion or env-name for the new key.
ABSENCE: search_files for REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR returns only docs/config.md and config.py — no test hit.
advisory.finding: The new config-loader wiring for parse_failure_artifact_dir (env REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR and the [tool.rebar.llm] TOML key) is untested: every new test sets cfg.parse_failure_artifact_dir directly on a constructed LLMConfig and none goes through LLMConfig.from_env, so a broken env-var name or _llm_str binding would not be caught.
scenarios: Env var name typo (e.g. renamed constant) or a broken _llm_str default silently disables the opt-in for operators who set it via env/TOML.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_config_llm.py, add REBAR_LLM_PARSE_FAILURE_ARTIFACT_DIR to the _clean tombstone list and a test asserting `_cfg(p).parse_failure_artifact_dir` picks up both the env var and a `parse_failure_artifact_dir = '/tmp/x'` TOML entry.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_rotation_keeps_only_the_newest_twenty, assert the newly written parse-failure-*.json artifact is present in the surviving set (e.g. one file matches the parse-failure prefix and is json.loads-able with the reply).
evidence: Assertions are `assert len(files) == 20` and `assert not oldest.exists()` only (tests/unit/test_structured_run.py:140-141)

The write-then-rotate contract keeps the newest 20 including the just-written path: `existing = sorted(d.glob('*.json'), key=... st_mtime); for stale in existing[:-20]: stale.unlink()` (src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:288-290)
advisory.finding: The rotation test verifies count==20 and that the oldest seeded file is evicted, but never confirms the newly written failure artifact survived rotation (it reads no survivor content), so it under-asserts the 'newest kept' half of the contract.
scenarios: A regression that writes the artifact after rotation, or unlinks the new file, would still leave 20 files and evict the oldest seed — passing the current assertions.

src/rebar/llm/errors.py:51-53 — CompletionRecoveryError: 'diagnostic is restricted to sanitized counters and references. It must never contain prompts, tool arguments/results, or model response text because callers may persist it in a gate-error sidecar.'
dropped.finding: The feature writes the raw model reply text verbatim to a local JSON artifact, which conflicts with the codebase's stated convention that persisted failure records must not carry model response text; the raw reply may echo prompt/source content, and no redaction or size cap is applied to the `reply` field.
scenarios: Operator opts in on a host where the configured dir is shared or later archived, capturing model output that may echo repository source or prompt content.
